result.instructions: SolidCraft is an independent parametric 3D CAD app, and these tools drive it: when its window is open the user watches the model appear, otherwise a headless session builds it. When asked to design or build a part (a bracket, an enclosure, a gear) do it with these tools straight away; nothing needs explaining first. Units are millimetres and degrees in expressions (internally radians), Z is up. Model like this: `sketch.create {plane: XY}`, draw (`sketch.rectangle.two_point {p0, p1}`, `sketch.circle.center {center, radius}`, `sketch.line {points, closed}`), constrain and dimension (`sketch.dimension {entities, value}`; values may name parameters), `sketch.finish`, then features (`solid.extrude {distance, operation?: new|join|cut|intersect}`, `solid.revolve`, `solid.fillet {edges: [[x,y,z] point on edge], radius}`, `solid.chamfer`, patterns, mirror, primitives). Use `batch` for several steps at once, `list_commands` for ids and parameter docs, `describe_command` for a command's schemas, `inspect_design` / `measure` to verify, `body_topology` to find edge points, `set_parameter` to drive the design and `screenshot` to look at it. A call whose error starts `still running:` was not cancelled: don't send it again; `pending` waits for its result. Backend: headless in-process SolidCraft session, because the SolidCraft app was not running when this server started; if it starts before any design work is done here, the next call is bridged to it.

tools.description: The command catalog: id, label, toolbar tab/panel, shortcut, one-line parameter docs and whether the command is enabled right now. Ids are dotted and lower-case (solid.extrude, sketch.create, solid.fillet, sketch.inspect, timeline.rollback). Optional case-insensitive substring `filter` over id, label, tab and panel (not the parameter docs, so a command id finds that command rather than every command whose docs mention it).
tools.name: list_commands
tools.title: List commands

tools.description: One command's parameter docs and, for commands with a typed contract (solid.box, solid.extrude and engine.describe so far), the JSON Schemas (2020-12) of its parameters (`input`) and of a successful result (`output`); null for the others.
tools.name: describe_command
tools.title: Describe a command

tools.description: Run one command with JSON parameters, exactly as the toolbar, palette and scripts do. Never opens a dialog. Examples: sketch.create {plane: "XY"}; sketch.rectangle.two_point {p0: [0,0], p1: [40,30]}; sketch.circle.center {center: [20,15], radius: 5}; sketch.dimension {entities: [curve id], value: "width"}; sketch.finish {}; solid.extrude {distance: 20, operation: "cut"}; solid.fillet {edges: [[0,0,10]], radius: 3}; solid.box {length, width, height}. Lengths are mm; expressions may use parameters and units ("width / 2", "30 deg"). Returns the command's result; failures leave the design unchanged. Sketch commands that add geometry return created: {points, curves, constraints, dimensions}: the ids of what they added, stable and not reused after a delete (undo rewinds the counters with the design), usable right away in sketch.dimension, sketch.constraint.* and sketch.delete. Feature commands return the feature's id and name, every body (bodies) and the bodies the feature created, changed and removed (created_bodies, changed_bodies, removed_bodies). view.pick {pixels: [[x,y]…]} answers the body, face, exact world point, normal and depth under pixels of a screenshot (read-only; docs/control-protocol.md).

verbose.description: false: omit the full feature body list and sketch ids repeated outside `created`; keep created_bodies, changed_bodies and removed_bodies (default true)

tools.name: execute
tools.title: Execute a command

tools.description: Run commands in order, stopping at the first error. Each step is {command, params}: an engine command id (as list_commands lists them). A step may also name one of these tools with that tool's arguments as params, and runs the engine command it stands for: set_parameter (parameters.change; `value` or `expression`), list_commands (engine.commands, with `filter`), describe_command (engine.describe), execute ({command, params}), measure (inspect.measure), inspect_design (document.inspect), undo, redo, export, save, open, new_design, crash_reports; screenshot, body_topology, batch and pending can't be steps. On an error the steps already run are undone (unless rollback: false), so the batch is all-or-nothing; the reply names the failing step (index from 0), its error, every result before it, whether the design really went back (rolled_back), the steps whose changes are in the design (applied) and those never sent (not_run). The usual way to build a part: sketch, draw, dimension, finish, extrude, fillet… in one call.

coalesce_parameters.description: Set each run of consecutive plain parameter edits (parameters.change or set_parameter with a name and a value, or changes) together, rebuilding the design once for the run instead of once per edit; a run that is refused goes step by step, naming the refused step. Other steps still see the design up to date. Each step keeps its own result; the run is one undo step (default false)

profile.description: Like timings, and each step's `profile`: {boolean_ms, tessellate_ms, other_ms}, its time in kernel booleans, in tessellation and the rest (default false)

rollback.description: Undo completed steps when one fails (default true)

timings.description: Add `timings`: [{index, command, ms}] for every step run (the failing one included) and `total_ms` (default false)

verbose.description: false: a compact reply. Feature steps leave out the full body list (created_bodies, changed_bodies and removed_bodies stay), sketch steps the ids they repeat outside `created` (default true)

tools.name: batch
tools.title: Run several commands

tools.description: The whole design: user parameters (expression, value, errors), the timeline (features with type, suppressed, rolled back, error, warning, timing), bodies (volume, area, centre of mass, bounding box, face/edge/vertex counts), sketches (curves with ids and coordinates, points, constraints, profiles, degrees of freedom, solve status), assembly joints (what each origin is attached to: occurrence, the feature, face, edge or sketch curve its face names refer to, whether it resolves and why not; `execute` `joint.inspect {joint}` gives one), the active sketch, selection and undo depth.

joints.description: Joint definitions as joint.inspect gives them, when the design has joints (default true)

sketches.description: Full sketch contents (default true; false = summary only)

tools.name: inspect_design
tools.title: Inspect the design

tools.description: Volume (mm³), surface area (mm²), centre of mass, bounding box and face/edge/vertex counts of one body or all bodies, with totals. With `items` (one or two selections, as `execute` takes them: faces, edges, vertices, sketch curves, profiles): one item's length, area or position, a circle's, arc's or cylinder's `diameter` and `radius` (with `circumference`, or an arc's `arc_length` and `angle_deg`), a slot's `slot` sizes; two items' `min` and `max` distance and, where one is round, `center_distance` (centre to centre, or from its axis).

items.description: One or two selections to measure instead of bodies, e.g. {"type": "face", "body": "Body1", "index": 3, "point": [x,y,z]}

tools.name: measure
tools.title: Measure bodies

tools.description: The edges (index, midpoint, length, endpoints) and faces (index, name, area, centroid, plane normal, a `point` that lies on the face, and for a cylindrical face its `cylinder`: origin, axis, radius) of a body. Use an edge midpoint as the [x,y,z] point that picks the edge for fillet and chamfer; a face's point or its name picks the face for the face commands.
tools.name: body_topology
tools.title: List edges and faces

tools.description: Create or change a user parameter and re-evaluate the timeline. `value` is a number (mm) or an expression ("40 mm", "width * 2", "30 deg"); `expression` is the same thing under the name the parameters.change command uses. Give one of the two (both only when they agree). Returns the new value, the features recomputed (`recomputed`), the features whose earlier result for the same inputs was reused instead (`restored`, e.g. after setting a value back) and any features that now fail.

comment.description: Comment shown in the parameters table

expression.description: Same as `value` (the parameters.change name); give one of the two

unit.description: mm, deg or "" (unitless); default from the expression

value.description: Number or expression (or give it as `expression`)

tools.name: set_parameter
tools.title: Set a parameter

tools.description: Render the design and return it as a PNG image. Headless: a CPU render of the model, fitted to the view. Connected to the app: a screenshot of the window (source "window", the default) or a render of the model with the app's camera (source "model"). Both show an active section (inspect.section) with its cut face capped. `view` first turns the camera to a standard view or a saved named view (view.save), `camera` to              any camera (as view.apply). `grid: false` and `axes: false` leave the ground grid (on Z 0) and the origin's axes out of a model render. A body whose appearance is see-through (appearance.assign with an `opacity` below 1) is drawn see-through, so what is inside it shows: that is how to look at the body a cut would remove inside the material it meets.

axes.description: false: leave the origin's three axes out of the render (see `grid`). Axes hidden with browser.visibility stay hidden

camera.description: Look from this camera instead: {target: [x,y,z], yaw, pitch, distance, fov?}                         (radians, mm; as view.save and view.apply)

grid.description: false: leave the ground grid out of the render. It lies on Z 0 and cuts through a part that straddles it. Model renders only: default true, or as the app shows it when connected; with `grid` or `axes` a connected screenshot is a model render, and source "window" is an error

height.description: Render height in pixels (model renders; default 600)

path.description: Also keep the PNG at this path

source.description: window = app screenshot, model = model render

view.description: Standard view (iso, home, front, back, top, bottom, left, right, fit) or the name of a saved named view                          (default: keep the current one; headless starts at iso)

width.description: Render width in pixels (model renders; default 960)

tools.name: screenshot
tools.title: Look at the design

tools.description: Export bodies to STEP (.step/.stp), 3MF (.3mf), binary STL (.stl), ASCII STL (format stla) or OBJ. The format comes from the extension unless given. URDF (.urdf) exports the whole assembly for robot simulators: a link per component placement with mass and inertia, joints from the assembly's joints, and STL meshes in metres written next to it (docs/urdf.md); RViz needs mesh_prefix such as package://robot/meshes/.

bodies.description: Body names (default: all; not with urdf)

effort.description: urdf: joint effort limit, N or N m (default 1000)

mesh_prefix.description: urdf: put before each mesh file name (default: none, so relative to the .urdf)

velocity.description: urdf: joint velocity limit, m/s or rad/s (default 10)

tools.name: export
tools.title: Export

tools.description: SolidCraft's crash reports on this computer (the app's when connected to it). Without `id`: the list, newest first (id, kind, time, message, command, count, version, path, replayable). With `id`: the whole report: message, location, backtrace, app version and commit, system, the command that crashed and the recent ones, and design_path / replay_path when it can be replayed: `solidcraft-cli crashes replay <id>`, or `solidcraft-cli run <replay_path> --in <design_path>`. Reports never leave this computer.

id.description: A report id from the list

tools.name: crash_reports
tools.title: Crash reports

tools.description: What the app is running or has queued right now, for every client: each request's connection and id, method, command id (a batch's step count), seconds since it arrived (running_s) and whether it still waits its turn (queued); `self` marks a request sent on the connection that asks. Answers at once, even while the app is busy, and never shows parameters. Ask it when a call timed out or the app seems slow, before sending a change again.
tools.name: running
tools.title: What the app is running

tools.description: Bridged to the app: the result of a request that was still running when its tool call returned (an error starting "still running:"). Waits for it up to 60 s: then its own result (or error), or done: false while it still runs (call again). pending: null when nothing is running. A request still running was not cancelled: don't send it again; other calls wait for it before they are sent.
tools.name: pending
tools.title: Result of a running request

tools.description: Undo the last change to the design.
tools.name: undo
tools.title: Undo

tools.description: Start a new, empty design (unsaved changes to the current one are discarded).
tools.name: new_design
tools.title: New design

tools.description: Open a .solidcraft design file, a STEP file (.step/.stp: a new design whose bodies come from the file, as an Import base feature in a component named after the file; an assembly's parts become nested components) or a mesh (.3mf/.stl/.obj/.glb/.gltf: mesh bodies in such a component; a glTF file's nodes become nested components and its materials appearances); the result reports the component (id, component_name). Replaces the current design; insert into it instead with the file.insert_step (STEP) or file.insert_mesh (mesh) commands. A STEP file from a system that has Y up opens lying on its back: `up: "y"` turns its component a quarter turn about X (Y becomes Z). glTF is Y up, so it is turned by default (`up: "z"` keeps its axes). `names` picks what the bodies are named after when the solids' own names say nothing useful.

names.description: STEP, IGES, FreeCAD and Rhino. auto (default): keep meaningful solid names, replace placeholders with the nearest named product, else instance; solid: the solid's own name; product: the part's name; instance: the occurrence's name, else the product's

up.description: STEP and glTF only. z keeps the file's axes; y: the file has Y up, so its bodies are turned to stand Z up. Default: z for STEP, y for glTF

tools.name: open
tools.title: Open a design

tools.description: Save the design to `path` or its current file. The default is a design container; a .json path selects plain JSON. Set format to container or json to override the path.

format.description: Design encoding (default: JSON for .json, container otherwise)

path.description: Path to save to (default: the current file)

tools.name: save
tools.title: Save the design

tools.description: Read a document of SolidCraft's bundled agent skills (solidcraft-modeling, solidcraft-mechanisms, solidcraft-editing, solidcraft-checking) from the copy built into SolidCraft. `file` defaults to reference.md; each skill also has SKILL.md. Unknown skills or files are refused with the available ones.

tools.title: Skill reference

# SolidCraft command reference for agents

These are the shapes of the commands a part build needs, so an agent rarely has to call `list_commands`. The worked example at the end runs in CI (`skill_reference_example_builds_as_documented` in `crates/mcp/src/tests.rs`).

- Lengths are in mm.
- Lengths take a unit suffix, in parameters and in feature fields: `"16 in"` is 406.4 mm, and `length:"1 in"` works in `solid.box`. `measure` still reports mm.
- Angles inside expressions take units: `"30 deg"`.
- Any numeric field can be an expression that names parameters: `"w/2 - wall - 6"`.

## Sketch planes: where sketch (x, y) lands in the world

| `plane` | sketch x | sketch y | normal (+distance) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `"XY"` | +X | +Y | +Z |
| `"XZ"` | +X | **-Z** | +Y |
| `"YZ"` | +Y | +Z | +X |
| `{origin, x_dir, y_dir}` | x_dir | y_dir | x_dir x y_dir |

- `offset: "expr"` on `sketch.create` moves the plane along its normal and follows parameters.
- **Front wall (-Y) of a part centred on the origin:**
  - Sketch on `{"plane":"XZ","offset":"-d/2"}`.
  - Draw a feature at height z at sketch y = **-z**.
  - A cut with a positive distance goes into the wall.
- **Top face:** sketch on `{"plane":"XY","offset":"h"}`.
- **Hole direction:** `solid.hole {sketch}` drills into the part from the face nearest the sketch. A hole sketch at z=0, or below the part, drills up into the bottom face. Put the sketch on the face the hole starts from.

## Ids

- **Numbering:** every creator returns `created: {points, curves, constraints, dimensions}`. Ids are stable and numbered per sketch.
- **Curves:** `l1`, `c1`, `a1`.
- **Points:** `p1`, `l1.start`, `l1.end`, `c1.center`, `a1.center`, and the sketch origin `"origin"`.
- **Rectangles:** `sketch.rectangle.*` also returns `sides {bottom,right,top,left}` and `corners {bottom_left,...}`.
  - `rectangle.center` adds 2 construction diagonals, so each corner joins 3 lines. Its centre point is `p5`.
  - `sketch.fillet {point}` therefore fails on its corners. Use `{a:"l1", b:"l4", radius}` or the 3D `solid.fillet`.
- **Slots:** `sketch.slot.overall` and `sketch.slot.center_to_center` create 2 lines, 2 arcs and 4 points, plus `a1.center` and `a2.center`. The ids count on from what the sketch already has: in an empty sketch `l1, a1, l2, a2` and `p1`-`p4`, after a `rectangle.two_point` `l5, a1, l6, a2` and `p5`-`p8`.
  - The `length` role of `slot.overall` is the overall length. The arc centres are at ±(length/2 - width/2).
  - After `length` and `width`, 3 dof remain. To remove them, dimension `origin` to `a1.center` horizontally and vertically, and `origin` to `a2.center` vertically. For a slot along Y the solver refuses that last dimension as over-constraining; dimension `a2.center` horizontally instead.
  - `sketch.slot.center_point` creates no centre point. Dimension an arc centre instead.
- **Circles:** `sketch.circle.center` creates `c1` and `c1.center`, and no `p` point.
- **Dimensions** share the `k` counter with constraints.
- **Constraints can add curves:** a constraint about an axis, such as `sketch.constraint.symmetry` with `line:"y"`, adds a construction line and so takes the next `l` id. Read `created` before you count further.
- **Over-constraining** is refused with `that conflicts with the sketch: neither entity can move to satisfy it`. For example, symmetry already makes two circles equal.

## Dimensions

```json
{"command":"sketch.dimension","params":{"entities":["origin","c1.center"],"type":"horizontal","value":"w/2 - wall - 6"}}
{"command":"sketch.dimension","params":{"entities":["c1"],"type":"diameter","value":"6"}}
{"command":"sketch.dimension","params":{"entities":["l1"],"value":"w"}}
{"command":"sketch.dimension","params":{"entities":["l1","c1"],"value":"2"}}
{"command":"sketch.dimension","params":{"entities":["c1","c2"],"value":"3"}}
```

A line, a point or another circle with a circle or arc measures to its edge (0 is tangent, or the point on the circle); two circles measure between their edges (the overlap when they cross, the thinnest wall when one is inside the other). Give the centre point (`c1.center`) for the distance to the centre.

Distances are unsigned. Draw the geometry on the correct side first, and the dimension keeps it there.

`sketch.draw.dimensioned` creates a shape and its dimensions in one undo step. The dimension roles depend on the creator:

| Creator | Roles |
|---|---|
| `line` (exactly 2 points) | `length`, `angle` |
| `rectangle.*` | `width`, `height` |
| `circle.*` | `radius` or `diameter` |
| `arc.center_point` | `radius`, `sweep` |
| `slot.center_to_center`, `slot.overall` | `length`, `width` |
| `polygon.*` | `radius` |

```json
{"command":"sketch.draw.dimensioned","params":{"command":"sketch.rectangle.center","params":{"center":[0,0],"corner":[35,25]},"dimensions":{"width":"w","height":"d"}}}
```

## Features

| Command | Minimal params | Traps |
|---|---|---|
| `solid.extrude` | `distance` | `profiles` defaults to **every region**, with a region inside another as a hole in it: two concentric circles give a ring. Pick regions with `[{"point":[x,y]}]` or `[index]`. Other options: `operation` (new/join/cut/intersect/auto), `direction` (positive/negative/symmetric), `through_all: true`, `start_offset`. A cut that misses reports success. |
| `solid.box` | `length`, `width`, `height` | `center:[x,y,z]` or `corner`. The quickest way to block out a part. `body_name` names the body it makes. With `operation:"cut"`, `targets:["Top"]` cuts only the bodies listed, so the cutter can pass through other bodies. |
| `solid.cylinder` | `radius` or `diameter`, `height` | `base` is the centre of the bottom (default origin), `axis` defaults to `Z`. Expressions work in `base`. Always pass `operation`. `body_name` and `targets` work as for `solid.box`. |
| `sketch.slot.overall` / `sketch.slot.center_to_center` | `p0`, `p1` (overall ends / arc centres), `width` | Ids and dof are in the "Ids" section above. |
| `solid.fillet` / `solid.chamfer` | `edges:[[x,y,z]]`, `radius` / `distance` | The pick snaps to the **nearest** edge. A pick farther than 5% of the body's size from every edge is refused, so check that the face count changed. One pick takes the whole tangent chain: a rounded rim needs 1 point, not 8. |
| `solid.shell` | `faces:[[x,y,z]]`, `thickness` | A point on each face to remove, or its name from `body_topology`. Fillet first, except an edge of a removed face or a fillet between curved faces (see Order in `SKILL.md`). Bodies with lofted or swept faces are refused (`offset: only bodies with planes, cylinders, cones, spheres and tori`): hollow a loft with a smaller loft and `operation: cut`. |
| `solid.hole` | `position:[x,y,z]` on a face (numbers or length expressions such as `["40", "width/2", "t"]`, which the hole then follows) + `diameter`, or `sketch` (+ `points`) | `clearance:"M3"`. `depth` defaults to through all. `type` is one of simple/drilled/counterbore/countersink. A `countersink` needs `cs_diameter` and `cs_angle`; a `counterbore` needs `cb_diameter` and `cb_depth`. `position` is a fixed point; to tie it to the part, add `references: [{edge:[x,y,z], distance}]` (up to two straight edges of the face): the centre then sits at those distances from the edges and follows them. |
| `solid.pattern.rectangular` | `features`, `dir1`, `count1`, `spacing1` (+ `dir2`, `count2`, `spacing2`) | Spacing takes expressions and follows parameters. |
| `solid.pattern.circular` | `features`, `axis` (`"Z"` or `{origin, dir}`), `count` | `angle` defaults to 360 deg. A full pattern keeps the COM on the axis, so check its radius with a top-view screenshot. |
| `solid.mirror` | `features:[names]` or `bodies:[names]`, `plane` (`XY`/`XZ`/`YZ`, a construction plane, or `{origin, normal}` whose origin may use length expressions) | Follows parameters. A mirror or pattern feature cannot be listed in `features` of another mirror or pattern, but `bodies` can mirror the body it made. The mirror is a new body with the first free default name: `Body1`, `Body2` from `features`, and `Side (2)`, `Side (3)` from `bodies:["Side"]`. Read the name from `created_bodies`. With `combine:true`, a mirror that overlaps the original joins it and makes no new body. `features` copies only the features listed, so a later cut is left out unless you list it too. `bodies` copies the finished body. To name the mirror, use `body.rename {"body":"Side (2)","name":"Side_L"}`. The new name stays when parameters change. |

- **Names:** name every feature (`"name":"Standoff"`) and keep names unique across sketches and features. `timeline.roll_to {"feature":"Plate"}` picks the first match, which can be the sketch.
- **Counts as parameters:** `parameters.add {"name":"n","expression":"6","unit":""}` creates a unitless parameter, and `"count":"n"` uses it in a pattern.
- **Holes on a parametric bolt circle:**
  1. Cut one hole with `solid.cylinder {"diameter":6.6,"height":"T + 2","base":["bcd/2",0,-1],"operation":"cut","name":"BoltHole"}`.
  2. Repeat it with `solid.pattern.circular {"features":["BoltHole"],"axis":"Z","count":"n"}`.

  Both the radius and the count follow their parameters.
- **Parameter changes:** for one change, call `set_parameter {"name":"L","value":"120 mm"}`. For several, use one `batch` of `parameters.change` steps instead of one `set_parameter` call each.
- **Primitive booleans:** a `solid.box` or `solid.cylinder` cut that touches curved faces of the target can fail with `the exact fallback ... takes planar faces only`. Use a sketch profile and an extrude cut instead, for example a slot sketch rather than a box plus 2 cylinders.

## Worked example: parametric plate with 4 counterbored holes (1 batch)

```json
{"commands":[
 {"command":"parameters.add","params":{"name":"L","expression":"80 mm"}},
 {"command":"parameters.add","params":{"name":"W","expression":"50 mm"}},
 {"command":"parameters.add","params":{"name":"T","expression":"6 mm"}},
 {"command":"parameters.add","params":{"name":"inset","expression":"8 mm"}},
 {"command":"sketch.create","params":{"plane":"XY","name":"PlateSketch"}},
 {"command":"sketch.draw.dimensioned","params":{"command":"sketch.rectangle.center","params":{"center":[0,0],"corner":[40,25]},"dimensions":{"width":"L","height":"W"}}},
 {"command":"sketch.finish","params":{}},
 {"command":"solid.extrude","params":{"distance":"T","name":"Plate"}},
 {"command":"solid.fillet","params":{"edges":[[40,25,3],[-40,25,3],[40,-25,3],[-40,-25,3]],"radius":5,"name":"Corners"}},
 {"command":"sketch.create","params":{"plane":"XY","name":"HolePts","offset":"T"}},
 {"command":"sketch.point","params":{"point":[32,17]}},
 {"command":"sketch.dimension","params":{"entities":["origin","p1"],"type":"horizontal","value":"L/2 - inset"}},
 {"command":"sketch.dimension","params":{"entities":["origin","p1"],"type":"vertical","value":"W/2 - inset"}},
 {"command":"sketch.finish","params":{}},
 {"command":"solid.hole","params":{"sketch":"HolePts","diameter":3.4,"type":"counterbore","cb_diameter":6.5,"cb_depth":3.3,"name":"Hole"}},
 {"command":"solid.pattern.rectangular","params":{"features":["Hole"],"dir1":[-1,0,0],"count1":2,"spacing1":"L - 2*inset","dir2":[0,-1,0],"count2":2,"spacing2":"W - 2*inset","name":"Holes"}}
]}
```

**Expected volume:**
- Plate: `L*W*T - 4*r²(1-π/4)*T`
- Each hole: `π*1.7²*(T-3.3) + π*3.25²*3.3`
- Total: 23335.2 mm³, with 22 faces.

After `set_parameter L=120` the volume is 35335.2 mm³, and the holes stay in the corners.

## Reading `measure`

- **Tolerance:** analytic and measured volumes agree to about 0.001-0.01%, so treat a gap that small as a match. Long shallow arcs measure worse, about 0.1% (R 1000 mm over 20 degrees).
- **Face counts:** compare the logical `faces`, not the larger `kernel.faces`.
- **Reply types:** `set_parameter` returns `recomputed` as a number. A batch reply echoes every step.
- **Boolean warning:** a feature `warning` such as `Boolean retry: temporary coincident-face separation up to 2.050000e0 mm per face` means the kernel nudged faces that coincide. A join flush on a face, such as a cylinder joined onto the floor of a shelled box, or a tapered cut that starts on a face, does not log it. When the volume still matches your number the warning is harmless. When it does not, the retry may have left the geometry wrong, with no error. A standoff built as a joined cylinder with a cut pilot hole, patterned together, reports `tool displacement` (moving a tool by about 2e-4 mm) but its volume agrees with the analytic growth; a boss with its hole as one ring profile (two concentric circles, extrude the ring) builds without a warning at every height tried (3 to 20 mm).

## Reply cost (0.8, plate example)

| Call | Size |
|---|---|
| `list_commands {}` | **Over 100 KB.** Never call it unfiltered; filter on a distinctive word such as `"hole"` or `"slot"`. |
| `body_topology` | 25-45 KB |
| `inspect_design {}` | 12 KB, and it grows with the sketches |
| `inspect_design {"measure":false,"sketches":false}` | 4 KB for one part: parameters, timeline errors, bodies. About 65 B more per body (14 KB at 210 bodies) |
| `sketch.inspect` | 5 KB per small sketch |
| `parameters.list {"filter":"feature"}` | 3 KB |
| `measure {}` | about 0.9 KB per body: volume, bbox, COM, face/edge/vertex counts. On a large design, `execute inspect.measure {"bodies":[...]}` measures only the listed bodies |
| `sketch.solve` | under 100 B: dof, status, profile count |
| `screenshot {"source":"model","width":480,"height":320}` | one small image. Without `source`, a bridged server returns the whole app window and ignores the size. |

## Errors

| Error text | Fix |
|---|---|
| `... is not available right now: no sketch is being edited` | Run `sketch.create` or `sketch.edit {sketch}` first. |
| `unknown sketch entity 'p1'` | Use the ids from `created`. A circle's centre is `c1.center`. |
| `the corner must join exactly two lines` | It is a `rectangle.center` corner. Use the `{a, b}` form. |
| `` `cs_diameter` must be a number or an expression `` | Countersinks need `cs_diameter` and `cs_angle`, even with `clearance`. |
| `unsupported dimension role for this creator` | Check the roles table above. |
| `<Feature> cannot be patterned or mirrored yet` | Pattern the original feature, for example one 2x2 rectangular pattern. |
| `an edge is a point [x,y,z], {point} or {body, index}` | An edge pick contained an expression. Use plain numbers. |
| `boolean Cut: the operation failed ... planar faces only` | See "Primitive booleans" above. |
